title: David Alfaro Siqueiros's birth chart
metaDescription: David Alfaro Siqueiros's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 8.6° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the ten placements whose signs are settled, fixed leads with four. Fixed signs hold the middle of their seasons, and a fixed-heavy chart is read as one that consolidates and does not easily let go.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Capricorn, but precisely: 8.6°, first decan, 0°–10°, under Saturn in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 25.6° Capricorn, Venus was at 20.3° Aquarius, Mars was at 13.6° Gemini. Read together: a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste led by wit and proportion; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Saturn to Uranus is the closest call of the day, a conjunction within 0.3°. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line. Behind it, Mercury sextile Saturn at 1.4°, and Mars conjunction Pluto at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Moon in Scorpio at 8.9° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Virgo at 10.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 air, 3 earth, 3 water by element and 4 fixed, 4 mutable, 2 cardinal by mode. An air-weighted chart thinks in through-lines; the sentence is how it takes hold of the world. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mars, Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.4° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 8.9°.
